prose: Anthropic's research post on agent memory borrows from neuroscience. The hippocampus captures experience quickly, and consolidation into long-term knowledge happens largely offline, during sleep. Agents can split work the same way: they log or transcribe their work, then use idle time to reflect on those logs to fix mistakes or write new notes. The idea builds on sleep-time compute proposed by Letta and UC Berkeley, and Anthropic calls the process dreaming. It says dreaming has helped it give Claude better memory. Only the opening was read.
highlights: Memory split: fast capture in logs, slow consolidation offline
Builds on Letta and UC Berkeley's sleep-time compute
